subject: Subprocessor change notice + redlined MSA/Order Form / DPA — Acme Cloud
messages:
From: Sophie Mendoza <sophie.mendoza@acmecloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: James Rhodes <j.rhodes@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Notice of subprocessor change + redlines attached

Hi Sean —

Per section 7 of our current MSA, Acme Cloud is notifying you that we will add a new analytics subprocessor (DataStream Inc.) for aggregated telemetry processing. Attached are redlined versions of the MSA and Order Form (minor edits), plus an updated DPA that includes the new subprocessor in Appendix A.

High-level:
- Effective date for the new subprocessor: 2027-08-01
- Data access: scoped to aggregated telemetry; no customer PII is shared
- We updated the indemnity cross-reference and added a short flow-down clause to the Order Form to ensure audit rights to the subprocessor.

Attachments: ACME_redline_MSA_20270718.pdf; ACME_OrderForm_redline_20270718.docx; ACME_DPA_subproc_list.xlsx

Can you confirm receipt and let us know if Redwood needs any additional information for legal review? We’re hoping to finalize before 2027-07-29.

Thanks,
Sophie Mendoza
Head of Procurement, Acme Cloud

Hi Sophie — thanks for the heads up and for sending the redlines. Confirmed received. I’ve looped in our legal and contracts team to review the MSA/DPA redlines — Kar (legal) and Monica (contracts) will scope the changes and get back with any required edits or questions.

For planning: we’ll aim to respond with a consolidated set of comments by end-of-day 2027-07-21. If anything appears material (e.g., expanded audit rights or new data categories), we may need a short follow-up call.

Neha — can you flag this in the deal record and sync timing with the renewal team?

Sean Gallagher

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Mendoza <sophie.mendoza@acmecloud.com>, James Rhodes <j.rhodes@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice of subprocessor change + redlines attached

Sean / team — I reviewed the redlines you sent. High-level comments below (quick summary before we produce a tracked redline back to Acme):

1) Subprocessor flow-down language (Order Form): Acme’s added clause gives them audit rights to the subprocessor; we need to ensure the flow-down is limited to the specific data processing activities related to telemetry and includes a 30-day notice to Redwood before exercising on-site audit rights. We should also require that any audit be performed at the subprocessor’s expense and that audits avoid disruption to production systems.

2) DPA Appendix A (subprocessor list): The new entry for DataStream Inc. does not include the subprocessor’s SOC/ISO attestations or relevant contact for security inquiries. Ask Acme to provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report and a designated security contact.

3) Indemnity and liability cross-references: The redline tweaks the cross-reference and tightens a limitation of liability exception for security breaches. That’s material — propose keeping cap language symmetric and add carveouts only where necessary (e.g., willful misconduct).

4) Encryption / key management: If DataStream will process telemetry that could include customer identifiers in edge cases, we should require that DataStream supports AES-256 at rest and TLS1.2+ in transit; if they manage keys, we need a KMS attestation or equivalent.

5) Subcontracting approvals: Acme is proposing a standard notice instead of prior written consent. For first-tier analytics subprocessors we accept a notice model if they: (a) certify the subprocessor meets our security baseline, (b) provide SOC/ISO docs, and (c) provide a 30-day notice. Anything beyond first-tier or if the subprocessor handles customer PII should require prior written consent.

Action items: Monica — please draft tracked redlines for the Order Form and DPA that: (i) narrow flow-down language, (ii) add an audit process limitation, and (iii) request SOC/ISO docs and security contact. I’ll draft the legal rationale and a short approval note to send to Acme.

-Karthik
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Mendoza <sophie.mendoza@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T14:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice of subprocessor change + redlines attached

Team — I prepared tracked changes and a short comment memo. Summary: we accept the subprocessor change with the following pre-conditions to be reflected in the Order Form / DPA:
- Acme to provide SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate for DataStream Inc. and a named security contact.
- Limit on audit execution: remote evidence collection + one on-site audit per 12 months, at Redwood’s discretion and the auditor must be mutually agreed.
- Notice model is OK for tier-1 analytics subprocessors only; any subprocessor with access to customer identifiers requires prior written consent.
- Maintain symmetric liability caps; do not accept unilateral expansion of indemnities.

I’ve uploaded our redline (Redwood_response_Subproc_20270720.docx) to the DocuSign link and added a short summary in the HubSpot deal notes. Sophie — please review the tracked changes; I called out the exact paragraphs to keep the scope tight.

Attachments referenced: Redwood_response_Subproc_20270720.docx (tracked)

Monica Patel
Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
From: James Rhodes <j.rhodes@acmecloud.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice of subprocessor change + redlines attached

Monica / Karthik — thanks for the quick review and clear summary. We appreciate the level of detail. Two quick notes:

1) We can provide SOC 2 Type II for DataStream and the security contact by tomorrow.
2) Regarding audits — Acme prefers to retain the right for supplier audits that are reasonable; we’re open to agreeing a narrow remote-first audit process with one on-site per year as a compromise.

If it helps, we’re happy to take your tracked redline and do a short 30-minute call to close outstanding items (availability tomorrow 10am PT or Friday 9am PT). Otherwise we’ll review your DocuSign redline and respond in-line.

Best,
James Rhodes
Sr. Contracts Manager, Acme Cloud
